questions.question: A flagship model wins procurement on benchmark quality, then costs 11x for two locked-in years. What would have prevented that?
options: A bigger benchmark number
Trust in flagship tiers generally
Faster procurement with less review
Feasibility gates plus year-two cost and exit modeling
questions.explanation: Quality signals are not procurement decisions. This lesson gates on feasibility, then scores total cost including exit.

questions.question: Which catalog platform remains feasible for an EU-resident interactive workload that requires open weights?
options: Groq API - Llama 4 Maverick
Azure AI Foundry (Germany West Central) - Claude Fable 5
Anthropic API direct (Claude Sonnet 4.x)
Self-hosted Llama 4 Scout (on-premise GPU)
questions.explanation: The workload requires both EU residency and open weights. The self-hosted entry supports EU, has open weights, and meets interactive latency; the other listed choices fail at least one gate.

questions.question: What model band does route_task select for a high-complexity, high-volume task?
options: BALANCED
FLAGSHIP
COMMODITY
No band, because high complexity is incompatible with high volume
questions.explanation: The high-complexity branch normally chooses FLAGSHIP, but high volume is explicitly cost-controlled to BALANCED. This avoids spending flagship rates on every high-volume call.

questions.question: What band does route_task select for a low-complexity task, regardless of its volume tier?
options: FLAGSHIP
COMMODITY
BALANCED
The same band as the preferred vendor
questions.explanation: After the high- and medium-complexity branches, route_task returns COMMODITY for low complexity. Volume affects the displayed monthly estimate, not this branch.

questions.question: What does the exit-cost-aware scorecard add to the procurement comparison?
options: A guarantee that the highest benchmark score wins
A second latency check that replaces compliance gates
A 25-point exit-cost axis based on data, code, eval, and compliance portability
A rule that excludes every proprietary platform
questions.explanation: AXIS_WEIGHTS assigns exit_cost 25 points, equal to monthly cost. The score averages four portability dimensions so migration risk is visible beside current run-rate.

questions.question: Which dimensions make up the five-axis score in score_platform?
options: Only capability, price, and benchmark rank
Residency, prompt length, training data, support tickets, and vendor age
Capability, price, and deployment region, with lock-in discussed separately
Cost, exit cost, compliance, latency, and preferred model-band match
questions.explanation: The weighted score combines cost, exit cost, compliance, latency, and band match. Feasibility gates handle residency and open-weight requirements before these axes are scored.
